title: observability-driven-runtime-refinement-playbook-2027
author: Riley Chen
content:
Purpose and scope:

This playbook documents the observability-driven refinement loop we use to continually improve the serving runtime (runtime-serving), kernel dispatch/scheduling (kernel-dispatcher), and associated subsystems (kv-cache-proxy, gpu-dispatcher, request-orchestrator). It ties together profiling, targeted benchmarks, safe release gating, runbook updates, and knowledge-base guidance. Use this document when proposing and validating runtime changes that can affect latency, throughput, cost-per-token, or stability.

Audience:
- Runtime engineers
- SREs and on-call responders
- Performance and ML infra teams doing model-onboarding
- Release owners and QA engineers

High-level refinement loop (summary):
1) Detect signal: alert or KPI drift (telemetry).
2) Hypothesize root cause: profiling + lightweight experiments.
3) Validate with targeted microbenchmarks and mixed-workload benchmarks.
4) Implement change behind feature flag / kernel variant.
5) Canary rollout with observability gating and automated rollback.
6) Post-deploy regressions analysis and runbook + docs update.

Key signals and canonical queries:
- Latency SLOs we watch (short-reqs < 128 tokens): p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 400ms.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) per GPU slot and per tenant.
- Kernel failure rate (kernel_dispatcher.error_count / kernel_dispatcher.invocations) < 0.1%.
- KV cache miss rate: kv_cache_proxy.miss_rate < 5% for steady-state traffic.
- Memory pressure events: node_memory_pressure{component="gpu"} > 0 => immediate page.

Example PromQL snippets (copy/paste):
- p95 request latency (short-reqs):
  quantile_over_time(0.95, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket{request_type="short"}[5m])) by (le))[15m:1m])
- kernel error rate: sum(rate(kernel_dispatcher_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kernel_dispatcher_invocations_total[5m]))
- kv cache miss rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))

Ownership and escalation map:
- Observability lead (owner): Riley Chen (runtime-observability).
- Kernel scheduling and execution: kernel-dispatcher team (owner alias: team-kernel).
- Oncall escalation: pager -> oncall-runtime -> team-kernel -> infra-leads.
- SLA/Customer-facing incident escalation: follow eng-sre incident-process.

Step-by-step investigation pattern (triage checklist):
1) Confirm signal and scope:
   - Use trace sampler IDs to map affected requests (trace_id prefix in logs).
   - Confirm whether problem affects a single tenant, model, or global pool.
2) Capture a short-profile snapshot (5–30s):
   - Run lightweight eBPF sampling on the node hosting the observed requests.
   - Capture kernel_dispatcher traces and per-kernel GPU timelines.
   - Collect kv-cache metrics and cold-start counts.
   - Commands (developer sandbox):
     - ./tools/trace-capture --node $NODE --duration 15s --out /tmp/trace.json
     - python tools/trace-annotate.py /tmp/trace.json --enrich telemetry:request_tags
3) Localize the hotspot: CPU vs GPU vs I/O vs kernel sync points.
4) Run targeted microbenchmarks (same model + sequence length profile):
   - Example command: ./bench/run_model_bench --model $MODEL --seq 64 --batch 1 --kernels=experimental
   - Compare against baseline run (use same runner and node type).
5) If kernel issue suspected, switch to a safe kernel variant behind a flag and repeat the benchmark.
6) Prepare rollout plan if improvement validated.

Profiling playbook: sampling, instrumentation and cost control:
- Sampling strategy: stratified sampling by request_size_bucket (short, mid, long), tenant_tier (free, standard, dedicated) to preserve signal across distributions. Target sample rate: 2–5% globally, 10–20% for canary lanes.
- On-node collection: use coordinated eBPF + CUDA timelines to minimize perturbation; prefer lightweight stack unwinds and kernel stage markers.
- Annotate samples with decision-trace fields: model_id, model_variant, prompt_hash_bucket, kv_cache_hit, kernel_variant. These fields are used by downstream attribution.
- Cost budget: a profiling job should not exceed 5% extra GPU overhead for production nodes; heavy profiling must be run on mirrored shadow nodes or in an offline lab.

Benchmarking integration (how to validate at scale):
- Microbench: single-model, controlled concurrency, fixed sequences. Use bench/run_model_bench to produce per-kernel timings and per-token cost.
- Mixed-workload suite: use the operational-workload-simulator (owsim) with recorded request traces to produce realistic tail behavior.
- Regression criteria: for any candidate change we require:
  - p95 short-req latency not worse by >5% absolute or 10% relative (whichever is smaller).
  - p99 latency not worse by >8% absolute or 15% relative.
  - throughput (tokens/sec per GPU slot) not worse by >6%.
  - kernel_error_rate stays below 0.1% and does not increase >2x baseline.
  - cost-per-token (in $-equivalent) not higher than baseline by >4% unless accompanied by quantifiable quality/latency gains.

Safe rollout recipe (gating and automation):
1) Feature flag + staging lab verification.
2) Canary lane: 0.5% of traffic for 24h with elevated sampling (10%). Gate checks at 1h, 6h, 24h.
3) Gradual ramp: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%; each step minimum 2h and must pass automated checks.
4) Automated gate checks (first 5 minutes and continuously):
   - Latency: short-req p95 within allowed delta.
   - Error counts: kernel_dispatcher_errors_total must be steady or declining.
   - CPU/GPU saturation: no node exceeds 92% sustained GPU utilization for 10m.
   - KV miss spikes: no jump >3x baseline.
5) Rollback policy: immediate rollback if any automated gate fails or on-call requests rollback.

Release notes and documentation checklist (for any runtime/kernal change):
- Summarize change in plain language (what, why, risk).
- List impacted services and owners.
- Add regression benchmark results (microbench + mixed-workload).
- Provide PromQL queries used for gating.
- Update runbooks: add a short triage flow and which flags to flip for rollback.
- Update team-wiki entries and attach trace examples.

Runbook updates and knowledge transfer:
- Every change that alters observability signals or runbook steps must include:
  1) Updated runbook snippet (what to check).
  2) Minimal repro steps and a link to a trace sample.
  3) Point of contact for follow-up.
- Example runbook snippet to add when kernel variants are introduced:
  - Symptom: increased p99 for long-requests.
  - Quick check: curl -s "${PROM_GATEWAY}/api/v1/query?query=<p99-query>"
  - Temporary mitigation: set feature flag kernel_variant=stable in rollout-service for affected pool.

Known issue cataloging (how to file and annotate):
- Use the runtime-known-issues label prefix and add the following fields in the ticket: reproducibility (always/rare/intermittent), affected-tenants (list), sample-trace-id, suggested-mitigation, root-cause-hypothesis, bench-results.
- Tag issues that require customer communication as customer-impacting and follow the escalation-playbook chain.

Observability hygiene and telemetry contract (must-haves):
- All kernels must emit: kernel_variant, kernel_latency_ms_{p50,p95,p99}, kernel_launch_failures, kernel_queue_depth.
- Request-level traces must include: request_id, trace_id, kernel_sequence, kv_cache_status, model_variant.
- Telemetry retention: full traces retained for 90 days for on-call purposes; aggregated histograms retained for 2 years for trend analysis.

Operational experiments and when to run them:
- Kernel A/B experiments: when a kernel variant improves microbench but uncertain at scale. Use canary lanes + mixed-workload benchmarks.
- Admission-control policy changes: require synthetic-chaos-stress profiles to validate tail behavior under contention.
- KV cache tuning: run shadow-caching experiments and measure miss-rate / cold-start frequency over 24 hours.

Templates and artifacts to attach to PRs or RFCs for runtime changes:
- Microbench summary CSV (include: model, seq_len, batch, kernel_variant, p50,p95,p99, throughput, gpu_util, cost_tokens_usd).
- Mixed-workload report (OWSim config, input trace id, result dashboard link).
- Trace samples (1 canonical trace for failure, 1 for normal).
- PromQL gating queries and expected thresholds.

Cross-team coordination and sign-off matrix:
- Required reviewers: team-kernel, runtime-observability, eng-sre, product (if customer-facing SLA change).
- Security review required if change affects encryption/tenant-isolation (eng-security).
- Dedicated capacity customers: product + customer-success must approve changes that change observed p95 by >10%.

Appendix A — Example microbench report (CSV snippet):
model,seq,batch,kernel_variant,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,throughput_tps,gpu_util,cost_token_usd
redwood-small,64,1,stable,18,42,90,1200,36,0.000012
redwood-small,64,1,experimental-fast,16,39,85,1280,38,0.000011

Appendix B — Quick diagnostic checklist for oncall (1–5 minute flow):
1) Check alert details and time window.
2) Confirm percent of traffic impacted (PromQL).
3) Collect 30s trace sample and tag as incident:<ID>.
4) Flip to kernel_variant=stable for pool if available and escalate if no immediate improvement.
5) If rollback occurs, schedule follow-up postmortem and run targeted microbench.

Appendix C — Useful CLI snippets and paths:
- Trace capture: ./tools/trace-capture --node $NODE --duration 15s --out /tmp/trace.json
- Run microbench: ./bench/run_model_bench --model $MODEL --seq 64 --batch 1 --kernels=${KERNEL_VARIANT}
- Canary control (internal API): curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/pool/alpha","flag":"kernel_variant","value":"stable"}' https://controlplane.internal/api/rollout

Final notes:
This playbook is intended to be pragmatic — make conservative changes in the hot path, validate with both lab and production-weighted benchmarks, and keep the on-call team empowered to rollback quickly. Update this page after every major runtime release (append release notes) and add any new gating queries or benchmark artifacts to the related_pages list.
